conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. You’re here because of worsening abdominal pain and nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it started with my usual back pain, then it moved to my stomach. I couldn’t keep anything down, not even my blood pressure pills.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And this happens about once a month, you said in the ER?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, the back pain flares up, then my stomach just shuts down. It’s like a cycle. I get anxious, then the nausea gets worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. Your history of gastroparesis and anxiety probably plays into this. We’ll focus on controlling the pain and nausea so you can eat again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I was in so much pain earlier, but the medicine in the ER helped a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. Your vitals are stable now. We’re starting IV fluids because you’ve been dehydrated from not eating. We’ll also keep an eye on your blood sugar.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My sugar was low in the ER, right? They gave me D50.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it was 70, which is low. But it’s stable now. No signs of ketoacidosis, which is good. We’ll continue your regular insulin regimen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ve been trying to stick to my 70/30 insulin. My A1c was 9.3 last time, so I know I need to do better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s actually an improvement. We’ll keep supporting you with your diabetic diet and sliding scale insulin as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about my blood pressure? I haven’t taken my lisinopril in days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You were hypertensive when you came in—144 over 105. We gave you one dose of lisinopril, and it helped. But we’re watching your kidney function closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My kidneys again? I’ve had issues before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your creatinine was 2.0 when you arrived, which is high for you. It’s come down a bit to 1.8, but not as much as we’d like.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that from not drinking enough? Or is my diabetes getting worse?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s likely a mix—dehydration from poor intake, but also possible progression of diabetic nephropathy. We’ve stopped lisinopril for now because it can affect kidneys when they’re stressed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh. So what will I take instead?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re starting amlodipine, a different blood pressure medicine that’s safer for your kidneys right now. You’ll take it daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. I’ll need to follow up with my doctor about this?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’ve already contacted your PCP to set up urgent follow-up with nephrology. They’ll check your kidney function and adjust meds if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I worry about my kidneys a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Totally understandable. We’re being proactive. Now, about your abdominal pain—your KUB scan showed no blockage or free air, which is reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not appendicitis or something like that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, nothing like that. There’s an air-fluid level in your stomach, which fits with gastroparesis—your stomach isn’t emptying well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s what usually happens. Can I try eating something now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You tolerated clear liquids in the ER, so we’ll start with a light meal. We’ll go slow—small portions, easy to digest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m really hungry. I haven’t eaten in two days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I know. We’ll get you something soon. We’re also giving ondansetron and ativan for nausea, and continuing your omeprazole for reflux.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been using ativan for anxiety and nausea. It helps.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and we’ll keep your usual lorazepam doses. We’re also continuing risperidone for your mood, as you’ve been seeing your psychiatrist regularly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, Dr. ___ has been helping me a lot. The psychotic features have been better lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great to hear. We’ll keep supporting your mental health. Your ECG showed sinus tachycardia—fast heart rate—but that’s likely from pain, anxiety, and being a bit dehydrated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My heart’s been racing. I thought it was anxiety.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s a mix. But your heart rate is coming down with fluids and symptom control. No need for extra meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You slept well, I hear. How’s your stomach today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Much better. I ate toast and applesauce last night and didn’t feel sick.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s excellent progress. We’ll advance your diet to regular food today. Still some nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Just a little, but not bad. I used the PRN ativan last night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’re minimizing narcotics to avoid constipation. You’re walking, blood pressure is better—102 over 50 now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s low, isn’t it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s on the lower side, but you’re not dizzy or weak. Amlodipine can lower it, so we’ll monitor. Your heart rate is 107—still a bit high, but improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel calmer today. Less anxious.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s helping your body recover. We’ll plan for discharge tomorrow if you keep doing this well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’d be great. I just want to get back to my routine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re officially discharged today. You’ve been eating full meals, pain is controlled, and labs are stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great news. What do I need to do when I get home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Continue all your usual meds except lisinopril—we’ve replaced it with amlodipine. Take it daily for blood pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And follow up with my PCP about my kidneys?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and they’ll refer you to nephrology. Also keep seeing your psychiatrist and monitor your blood sugar closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for helping me through this flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Call if the pain or nausea comes back, or if you can’t keep fluids down. Otherwise, take care.
